data.description:
## Context / Problem
The docs overlay reviewer tags all its findings docs-only (src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-docs.md:19); routing gives docs `nit_suppressed: true` and `blocking_enabled: false` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json:57-68); post-Pass-3 nit suppression (src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:426-446) demotes every docs-only advisory. Net: 100% of the overlay's verified-valid output is discarded — 47 of 125 nit-suppressed findings had validity >= 0.8 AND impact > 0 (e.g. a CONTRIBUTING.md path list factually wrong vs the checker). Separately, 95 findings were absence-speculation ("file may not exist") from the tool-less overlay, correctly refuted at Pass-2 but billed.

## Approach
Two changes: (1) make nit suppression impact-aware at workflow_ops.py:443-446 — suppress a docs-only advisory only when its impact is 0; findings with impact > 0 surface as advisories. (2) Narrow code-review-docs.md: report only inconsistencies where the diff itself shows both sides; explicitly forbid emitting "must exist / may be stale / should be verified" speculation about files not in the diff. Alternative rejected: dropping nit_suppressed from routing entirely — re-admits the 61 zero-impact nits the suppression correctly removes.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py, src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-docs.md, tests/llm/test_code_review_nit_suppression.py.

## Testing
Unit on the Pass-3/post-decide pipeline with fixture findings: docs-only + impact 0.3 survives as advisory; docs-only + impact 0 suppressed; multi-criteria behavior unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A docs-only advisory with impact > 0 survives nit suppression and surfaces (checked: pipeline unit test).
- [ ] A docs-only advisory with impact == 0 remains suppressed (checked: pipeline unit test).
- [ ] code-review-docs.md contains an explicit prohibition on absence speculation about files not shown in the diff (checked: test asserts the rubric text contains the prohibition).
data.title: docs code-review findings are structurally unsurfaceable
